methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone, a publicly listed company on the Tokyo exchange, operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The company completed an IPO as its most recent financing event. The comparable universe for this analysis consists of six private companies in the Drones & Autonomous space, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public peers in the narrow sector exist at a comparable stage or valuation tier.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable to this valuation. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains five total peers, but filtering by stage, adjacent-stage classification, or similar valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any single category. A median derived from the entire sector would introduce substantial methodological bias given the heterogeneity of business models, geographies, and maturity levels within the peer set. Consequently, this approach was rejected rather than force-fit to insufficient data.

Given the absence of sufficiently granular comparable data and Terra Drone's unique position as the only public company in this narrow peer universe, traditional valuation triangulation cannot be reliably executed. A complete valuation assessment would require either (1) expansion to adjacent sectors with comparable unit economics, (2) primary transaction data from recent fundraises among the identified private peers, or (3) bottom-up discounted cash flow analysis grounded in specific revenue and margin assumptions for the Tokyo market. Current data constraints preclude a defensible range estimate.
